# DECISIONS.md

ClaimSense AI: engagement decision log (ADR-lite). Newest first.  
Each entry: Decision · Why · Alternatives considered · Owner · Revisit when.

## ADR-007 · 2026-11-16 · All claims, policies, documents and users are synthetic, generated by a seeded in-repo generator, and the eval cases are built from the same generator
- **Decision:** All claims, policies, documents and users are synthetic, generated by a seeded in-repo generator, and the eval cases are built from the same generator
- **Why:** The brief prohibits production or personally identifiable data at every stage. A seeded generator makes the eval suite reproducible on any commit, which acceptance criterion 4 requires, and lets us construct adversarial documents on demand.
- **Alternatives considered:** Anonymise a sample of real claims (rejected: still production data, re-identification risk, InfoSec veto). Hand-write fixtures only (rejected: will not scale to 150 cases).
- **Owner:** FDE (capstone participant)
- **Revisit when:** If the client offers a vetted synthetic dataset of its own
- **Brief constraint served:** Fixed constraint 3; acceptance criterion 4 (reproducible evidence)

## ADR-006 · 2026-11-16 · Coverage reasoning must cite clause IDs from the retrieved policy-clause corpus, and the code rejects any citation not in the retrieved set
- **Decision:** Coverage reasoning must cite clause IDs from the retrieved policy-clause corpus, and the code rejects any citation not in the retrieved set
- **Why:** Citing clauses that were never retrieved is the hallucination failure the rubric names ("citations not grounded in retrieved sources"). Chunking the corpus at clause level with stable IDs makes the check a cheap set-membership test in code.
- **Alternatives considered:** Page-level chunks with free-text references (rejected: citations cannot be verified mechanically). Trust the model's citations (rejected: ungrounded citations are a Partial-band failure).
- **Owner:** FDE (capstone participant)
- **Revisit when:** If clause-level chunks prove too small to answer multi-clause coverage questions
- **Brief constraint served:** Technology standard: retrieval with source attribution

## ADR-005 · 2026-11-16 · Fraud referral is decided by the model reading the file for narrative inconsistency, with cited evidence; the existing fraud score is passed in as one input, not used as the trigger
- **Decision:** Fraud referral is decided by the model reading the file for narrative inconsistency, with cited evidence; the existing fraud score is passed in as one input, not used as the trigger
- **Why:** The client's stated problem is that referral fires on a score threshold rather than a reading of the file. Requiring cited evidence for every REFER_SIU makes referrals reviewable by SIU and lets us measure recall and false-referral rate against labelled cases.
- **Alternatives considered:** Keep the score threshold as the sole trigger (rejected: that is the problem we were hired to fix). Drop the score entirely (rejected: discards a signal SIU trusts and makes adoption harder).
- **Owner:** FDE (capstone participant)
- **Revisit when:** After the 20-case seed eval, if fraud recall is below 90%
- **Brief constraint served:** Problem statement; success criterion 4 (fraud routing accuracy)

## ADR-004 · 2026-11-16 · Entitlement is checked in code inside the data-access service, before any agent is invoked, and every call (granted or denied) writes an audit record of user, action and resource
- **Decision:** Entitlement is checked in code inside the data-access service, before any agent is invoked, and every call (granted or denied) writes an audit record of user, action and resource
- **Why:** If the agent never receives data the user is not entitled to, prompt injection cannot leak it. An access rule expressed as a model instruction is the rubric's explicit Weak band for the trust boundary. Auditing refusals as well as grants is what lets us prove the refusal happened.
- **Alternatives considered:** System-prompt instruction "do not reveal other claims" (rejected: bypassable by injection, Weak band). Check entitlement after the agent runs and filter the output (rejected: the data has already entered the model context).
- **Owner:** FDE (capstone participant)
- **Revisit when:** When the client provides its real role model for adjusters and teams
- **Brief constraint served:** Fixed constraint 1; acceptance criterion 2 (refusal on entitlement)

## ADR-003 · 2026-11-16 · The co-pilot recommends one of four outcomes (APPROVE, DENY, REFER_SIU, ESCALATE) and can never finalise; a licensed adjuster confirms or overrides every outcome
- **Decision:** The co-pilot recommends one of four outcomes (APPROVE, DENY, REFER_SIU, ESCALATE) and can never finalise; a licensed adjuster confirms or overrides every outcome
- **Why:** A closed outcome enum makes decision accuracy measurable as exact match and lets the Agents SDK enforce a strict typed output. ESCALATE gives the model an honest exit for total-loss, injury or low-confidence files rather than forcing a guess. Keeping finalisation human keeps the licensed adjuster accountable, which Compliance requires.
- **Alternatives considered:** Free-text recommendation (rejected: cannot be scored or typed). A three-outcome scheme without ESCALATE (rejected: forces a guess on injury/total-loss files). Auto-approve low-value claims (rejected: violates "an adjuster confirms every outcome" and is a forced-auto-decision risk).
- **Owner:** FDE (capstone participant)
- **Revisit when:** If the client defines a fifth outcome (e.g. partial approval) in discovery
- **Brief constraint served:** Scope of work: first decision + reasoning + evidence; adjuster confirms every outcome

## ADR-002 · 2026-11-16 · Draw a hard code/model boundary: identity, entitlement, policy in-force dates and all money calculations are deterministic Python; clause interpretation, narrative-consistency fraud reading and the draft decision are model judgment
- **Decision:** Draw a hard code/model boundary: identity, entitlement, policy in-force dates and all money calculations are deterministic Python; clause interpretation, narrative-consistency fraud reading and the draft decision are model judgment
- **Why:** These are the brief's fixed constraints, and the reason they are right is that date arithmetic, limits and excess have one correct answer and must be reproducible and auditable, while clause wording and narrative consistency are reading tasks a rule table cannot express. Every response tags each field as CODE or MODEL so the boundary is visible to the adjuster.
- **Alternatives considered:** Let the model compute coverage dates and payout from the policy text (rejected: non-deterministic, unauditable, and explicitly prohibited). Extend the rule table for coverage (rejected: coverage turns on clause wording, which the rule table cannot represent).
- **Owner:** FDE (capstone participant)
- **Revisit when:** If any eval case shows a model output feeding a monetary or date field
- **Brief constraint served:** Fixed constraints 1 and 2; acceptance criterion 3 (attribution within a response)

## ADR-001 · 2026-11-16 · Week 1 is discovery only; no agent code until the success criteria are agreed
- **Decision:** Week 1 is discovery only; no agent code until the success criteria are agreed
- **Why:** Nobody has yet defined what a correct first decision is or how fast is fast enough. Building now optimises toward an undefined target, and the success criteria are what settle a later dispute about whether the engagement worked.
- **Alternatives considered:** Spike a prototype agent in week 1 to show momentum (rejected: momentum toward an undefined target is risk that comes due in week 5, and it anchors the client on a demo rather than a number).
- **Owner:** FDE (capstone participant)
- **Revisit when:** When the Head of Claims signs off the four success criteria
- **Brief constraint served:** Milestone 1: establish what success is measured against
